channel.title: AI - Ars Technica
channel.description: Serving the Technologist since 1998. News, reviews, and analysis.

item.title: Google's new command-line tool can plug OpenClaw into your Workspace data
item.description: This could make it easier to use multiple Workspace APIs, but it's not yet an official Google product.

item.title: Musk fails to block California data disclosure law he fears will ruin xAI
item.description: Musk can't convince judge public doesn’t care about where AI training data comes from.

item.title: AI startup sues ex-CEO, saying he took 41GB of email and lied on résumé
item.description: Hayden AI also claims co-founder improperly sold over $1.2M in stock.

item.title: Workers report watching Ray-Ban Meta-shot footage of people using the bathroom
item.description: Meta accused of "concealing the facts" about smart glass users' privacy.

item.title: OpenAI introduces GPT-5.4 with more knowledge-work capability
item.description: Updates come amid user blowback over the company's Pentagon deal.

item.title: Large genome model: Open source AI trained on trillions of bases
item.description: System can identify genes, regulatory sequences, splice sites, and more.

item.title: Lawsuit: Google Gemini sent man on violent missions, set suicide "countdown"
item.description: Gemini allegedly called man its "husband," said they could be together in death.

item.title: Are consumers doomed to pay more for electricity due to data center buildouts?
item.description: Data center operators to sign pledge to supply their own power instead of relying on grid.

item.title: LLMs can unmask pseudonymous users at scale with surprising accuracy
item.description: Pseudonymity has never been perfect for preserving privacy. Soon it may be pointless.

item.title: Iowa county adopts strict zoning rules for data centers, but residents still worry
item.description: Though the rules are among the strictest in the US, locals say they aren't enough.

item.title: Trump moves to ban Anthropic from the US government
item.description: The Defense Department pressured Anthropic to drop restrictions on how its AI can be used by the military.

item.title: Block lays off 40% of workforce as it goes all-in on AI tools
item.description: CEO says "most companies are late" to realize how much technology will affect employment.

item.title: Perplexity announces "Computer," an AI agent that assigns work to other AI agents
item.description: It's also a buttoned-down, ostensibly safer take on the OpenClaw concept.

item.title: xAI spent $7M building wall that barely muffles annoying power plant noise
item.description: “Temu sound wall” not enough to quell fury over xAI’s power plant.

item.title: Google reveals Nano Banana 2 AI image model, coming to Gemini today
item.description: Google's new image model replaces the previous versions immediately.

item.title: Musk has no proof OpenAI stole xAI trade secrets, judge rules, tossing lawsuit
item.description: Even twisting an ex-employee's text to favor xAI's reading fails to sway judge.

item.title: The Galaxy S26 is faster, more expensive, and even more chock-full of AI
item.description: Samsung's Galaxy S26 series is available for preorder today and ships on March 11.

item.title: Pete Hegseth tells Anthropic to fall in line with DoD desires, or else
item.description: CEO was summoned to Washington after trying to limit military use of its technology.

item.title: Meta could end up owning 10% of AMD in new chip deal
item.description: AMD will supply 6 gigawatts' worth of chips to buttress Meta's AI efforts.

item.title: Data center builders thought farmers would willingly sell land, learn otherwise
item.description: Even in a fragile farm economy, million-dollar offers can't sway dedicated farmers.
